newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Verbund says full-year may exceed 1995.
newsitem.headline: Verbund says full-year may exceed 1995.

text.p: Austrian national utility Verbund said on Thursday full-year earnings may exceed last year's provided the coming winter months are sufficiently cold.
"Then we could see a better result than last year," chief executive Johann Haider told Austrian news agency APA.
He added that the company, which supplies almost two-thirds of Austria's energy needs, would aim at an unchanged dividend of 16 schillings.

Last year, Verbund posted a group net profit of 1.38 billion schillings. Net profit in the first six months of this year jumped 42 percent to 765.6 million schillings, while pre-tax climbed 35 percent to 864 million.
However, half-year operating profit was down 20 percent at 1.58 billion schillings as river levels fell and Verbund was forced to turn from cheap hydro electricity to thermal power.

Haider said the company, faced with the gradual opening of national energy markets over the next few years in line with European Union directives, aimed at cost savings of up to one billion schillings annually until the beginning of the next decade. Most of the savings would come from job cuts.
